items.name: your-component
items.title: Your Component
items.description: A placeholder component. Replace this with your custom shadcn component.

items.name: hero-section
items.title: Data panel hero
items.description: Marketing hero with a cluster of data panels, rolling CTAs and a logo wall that cycles on scroll.

useCases: SaaS and AI product landing pages
Analytics, data and dashboard products
Launch pages that need proof above the fold

a11y.reducedMotion: The entrance rise, the noise-field sweep and the sliding button labels and brackets are dropped (hover swaps happen instantly), and the logo wall stops cycling, showing one name per cell.

keyboard.action: Moves through the nav links and “Try for free” (below lg: “Try for free”, “Menu”, its links), then the hero links.
On “Menu” (below lg), shows or hides the nav links under the header.
In the open menu, closes it and returns focus to “Menu”.
Follows the focused link.

notes: The headline “Private company data and signals API” is an h1, with no prop to change its level, so the section should open the page.
Below lg a “Menu” button (aria-expanded) shows the same five nav links in a “Site” nav under the header; closed, they're hidden and out of the tab order.
Every call to action is a plain link; icons and the duplicate copy of each rolling label are aria-hidden, so each link is read once.
The noise-field ticks and sentiment bars are aria-hidden; a screen-reader sentence gives the figures (197 of 1,000 articles kept). The canonical record is a description list.
The flipping logo wall is aria-hidden, and a screen-reader line lists the customers once: KPMG, Adobe, JLL, Chicago Booth, BabyAGI.
gaps: The logo wall flips every 2.6–3.5 s for as long as it's on screen, with no pause control; only the reduced-motion setting stops it (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).

items.name: benchmarks-section
items.title: Competitor benchmarks
items.description: Four metrics against competitors, each drawn as its own chart: isometric bars, unit field, radar and stacked slabs.

useCases: Comparison pages: why you over a competitor
SaaS and developer-tool landing pages
Launch or investor pages that lead with numbers

a11y.reducedMotion: The header and the chart grid fade and rise in as they scroll into view; with reduced motion they are simply shown in place. Nothing else animates.
notes: The section heading is an h2, and each metric is an article whose title is an h3 with its qualifier, e.g. “F1 Score (accuracy × recall)”.
Each SVG chart is one image with a label such as “F1 Score by provider, isometric bar chart”, so its drawn labels aren't read one by one.

Under every chart a visually hidden list gives each provider and figure, e.g. “akta.pro: 81.3”, so the data doesn't depend on the drawing; the Accuracy unit field's visible rows are aria-hidden so nothing is read twice.
The metric icons and the eyebrow's square are hidden from screen readers.

items.name: team-section
items.title: Team avatar grid
items.description: Clustered avatars synced to a list of roles and bios.

useCases: About and company pages
Careers and hiring pages
Agency and studio team pages

a11y.reducedMotion: The rise and scale on entry, the hover lift, the press shrink and the role badge's slide are dropped, leaving fades. The photo's colour and dimming still change with a short transition.

keyboard.action: Moves through the six role rows, one stop per person; the avatar tiles are for the pointer only.
Selects that person: their photo turns to colour, the others dim, and their row is marked.

notes: The heading “The people behind the work” is an h2, with the eyebrow and the body as paragraphs.
Each role row is a button named by its own text, e.g. “Founder & CEO, Maya Ellis, Started the studio in 2019.”, with aria-pressed marking the chosen person.
The avatar tiles are `focusable={false}` here (a new AvatarGrid prop): not Tab stops and hidden from screen readers, since the rows offer the same choice.
Role icons, the centre logo mark and the empty hatched tiles are aria-hidden; below lg, the active person's name and role also show in a badge beside their tile.

items.name: tables-section
items.title: API keys table
items.description: Search, filters, row selection, pagination, and create, rotate and delete dialogs.

useCases: Developer platforms and API dashboards
Admin panels that manage keys or tokens
SaaS settings and account pages

a11y.reducedMotion: Under reduced motion the Refresh icon doesn't spin and the loading rows don't pulse; the 0.7 s refresh shows still placeholder rows. Menus and dialogs animate as your shadcn primitives do.

keyboard.action: Moves through the header links, search, filters and Refresh, then each row's checkbox, name, copy and actions.
Ticks or unticks a row's checkbox or “Select all rows on this page”.
Presses a button: a key's name opens “Edit API key”; Status, User, View and row actions open menus.
Moves through an open menu's items; Enter / Space picks one.
Closes an open menu or dialog.
In a dialog's field, submits it (Create, Save changes, Rotate key, Delete) once the input is valid.
With focus or the pointer in the table, outside text fields: create a key, refresh, open SDK, open Documentation.
With focus or the pointer in the table, jumps to the “Search API keys” field.

notes: The “API Keys” heading is an h2, and the keys sit in a real table with column headers; the last column's header is the screen-reader text “Row actions”.

Icon-only controls are named (“Refresh API keys”, “Copy prefix of production”, “Actions for production”, “Next page”), and each key's name button reads “Rename production”, though only “production” shows.
Row checkboxes are named “Select {key name}” and “Select all rows on this page” reports mixed; Create, Edit, Rotate and Delete open titled dialogs, focus starts in the name field.

Shortcuts never answer page-wide, and `shortcuts={false}` turns them off with their hints. The key hints are hidden from screen readers and exposed as `aria-keyshortcuts`, so names read “Create API key”.
A polite status line announces “Refreshing API keys.”, “Copied the prefix of production.” and, once a search or filter settles, how many keys match (“3 keys match.”).
gaps: The shortcuts also answer while the pointer rests over the table with focus elsewhere, and only the host (`shortcuts={false}`) can turn them off, not the visitor; kept so mouse users keep them (WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts).

items.name: tables-section-02
items.title: Support tickets table
items.description: Help-desk queue with saved views, live SLA timers, inline status, priority and assignee, sorting, CSV export and a ticket detail sheet.

useCases: Help-desk and customer-support tools
Internal ops and admin dashboards
SaaS apps with a filterable queue of records

a11y.reducedMotion: The ticket sheet fades in and out instead of sliding, and the refresh icon stays still during the 0.7 s refresh. Menus and dialogs keep the shadcn fade and slight zoom.

keyboard.action: Moves through Export, New ticket, the view tabs, search, Filter, View and Refresh, then each row’s controls
In the view tabs, moves to another view and shows it; in a menu, closes or opens a submenu
Moves through the items of an open menu
Activates the focused button or menu item; Space also ticks a checkbox
Closes the open menu, dialog or ticket sheet
Opens the New ticket dialog, only while focus is in the table and not in a field
Moves focus to “Search tickets”, only while focus is in the table
Refreshes the list, or exports the matching tickets as CSV, only while focus is in the table

notes: The section has an h2 “Support tickets”; the table uses real header cells, the sortable Priority and Due headers set aria-sort, and the actions column has a hidden “Row actions” header.
Cell menus are named per row, like “Status of TCK-1047”; unread subjects add a hidden “(unread)”. The shortcut letters are hidden from screen readers and exposed through aria-keyshortcuts.
The single-letter shortcuts answer only while focus is inside the section; clicking anywhere in it puts focus there (the section has `tabIndex={-1}`, so it is not a Tab stop).
A polite live region announces refreshes, exports, created and deleted tickets, copied links, and, after a search, filter or view change, how many tickets match, e.g. “12 tickets match.”
In New ticket, Subject and Email are `required` and the dialog’s description says “Subject and email are required.”; all fields have visible labels.

items.name: hero-section-02
items.title: Showreel wheel hero
items.description: A hero with your work on a turning film wheel: drag, swipe or use the keys to spin it, with a live caption and a scrolling client row.

useCases: Agency, studio and freelancer portfolios
Photographers', filmmakers' and creators' showreels
Brand sites that lead with their work

a11y.reducedMotion: The wheel's spin-in, the text rise and the logo marquee are off, autoplay stops, and the wheel jumps to the next frame instead of springing. Dragging still moves it under your finger.

keyboard.action: Moves to the frame at the crest of the wheel, then “Book a call” and “See how we work”.
Turns the wheel one frame back or forward; focus follows the new frame at the crest.
Follows “Book a call”, “See how we work”, or a reel's caption link when the reel has an `href`.

notes: The title is an h1 by default (h2 with `headingLevel={2}`). The wheel is a region labelled “Showreel” with the role description “carousel”.

Only the crest frame is in the Tab order: a button named by its reel's description, described by its picture's alt text, and marked aria-current. Only the crest's caption is exposed, with counts read as “YouTube views 1.2M”.
After the first interaction, a polite live region reads the new crest's description; autoplay steps before that are not announced.
The scrolling logo row is hidden from screen readers and replaced by one hidden sentence, “Trusted by: Figma, Slack, Supabase, …”.
gaps: The wheel advances every 5 seconds while on screen with no visible pause button; it only holds while the pointer is over it or a frame has focus. (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide)
The logo row loops without end and pauses only on mouse hover, with no pause control for keyboard or touch users. (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide)

items.name: testimonials-section
items.title: Metrics testimonials section
items.description: Customer stories with auto-scrolling progress timer, cross-fading quotes, and live KPI impact metrics.

useCases: SaaS and B2B landing pages
Sales, CRM and revenue tool websites
Customer story and case study pages

a11y.reducedMotion: Stories still advance every 6 seconds, but the progress bars are hidden and the arrows no longer nudge on hover or shrink when pressed. The quote, photo and figures still cross-fade (opacity only).

keyboard.action: Moves to “Previous testimonial”, then “Next testimonial”; under 640px they are hidden until one of them has focus.
Shows the previous or next story, restarts the timer and announces the new story.

notes: The heading is an h2 by default (`headingLevel` sets 1–3) and each quote is a blockquote.
The large portrait's alt names the person, role and company, e.g. “Marcus Vance, CEO & Co-founder at Vance Systems”; the small avatar shown on narrower screens uses just the name.
The arrow and trend icons are hidden from screen readers; each change is written out with its sign, e.g. “+14.6%”, so it doesn't rely on the icon or its green colour.
A polite status region reads the new story after a button press or swipe, e.g. “2 of 5: Elena Rostova, VP of Operations at Stratum Dynamics.” and the quote; automatic changes are not announced.
gaps: Stories advance every 6 seconds with no pause or stop control, and the timer doesn't hold on hover or focus. (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide)

Under 640px the arrow buttons show only on keyboard focus, so touch users without a keyboard or screen reader still change stories by swiping; showing them would change the phone design. (WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures)

items.name: image-sphere
items.title: Image sphere
items.description: Your images on a WebGL globe you can hold: fling it, click an image and its group lands in a labelled pile.

useCases: Portfolio and gallery pages
Agency and studio websites
Brand, product or campaign image showcases
Event and launch microsites

a11y.reducedMotion: The globe doesn't turn on its own and a fling stops dead; a group's images jump straight into the pile with no flight, toss or squash, and images appear without fading. Dragging still turns it.

keyboard.action: Moves through “All” and the seven group buttons, which appear over the sphere while one has focus.
Opens that group's pile; “All” puts the images back on the sphere.
Closes the open group while focus is in the block, and hides the hover tag.

notes: The block is a region named “Images by group”, and the WebGL canvas and the hover tag are aria-hidden.
The group buttons sit in a group named “Groups” and mark the open one with aria-pressed; when the parent controls `group`, these buttons are left out.
A hidden list gives screen readers the images by their alt text: every image, once, in a list named “Images on the sphere”, or the open group's pile, e.g. “Architecture images”.
Opening a group is announced politely, for example “Architecture: 12 images”.
Without WebGL2, a plain grid of images with their alt text replaces the sphere.
gaps: The globe turns continuously (one turn per 45 s by default) with no pause control; it stops only while a group is open, with autoRotate off, or under reduced motion (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).

items.name: hero-section-03
items.title: Artwork fan hero
items.description: A centred headline over a fanned row of artworks with a hand-drawn hint, a line of copy and two pill actions. A deck opens into the fan on load; hover or tap a card and it comes out and turns over in 3D to show the artist, title, medium and price. 4 cards on phones, 5 on tablets, 7 on desktops.

useCases: Art marketplaces and print shops
Creator, illustrator and designer platforms
Portfolio and gallery sites that lead with the work
Membership launches for creative communities

a11y.reducedMotion: The deck rising, the fan opening, the text rising and the hint drawing are all skipped, and transitions are off: cards still lift, part their neighbours and turn over, but instantly.

keyboard.action: Moves through the artwork cards (4 on phones, 5 on tablets, 7 on desktops), then “Sign up” and “Read more”.
Turns the focused card over to show the artist, title, medium and price; press again to turn it back.
Turns an opened card back.
Follows “Sign up” or “Read more”.

notes: The headline is an h1 by default (headingLevel={2} inside a longer page); the cards sit in a list named “Featured artworks”.

Each card is a button named by its image's alt text plus “by {artist}. Show details.”, e.g. “Pink and white flower painting by Hana Sato. Show details.”, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at its back.

A card's back is aria-hidden until it's turned over; then it reads the artist, handle, “Artwork”, title, medium and year, price and status, all as text (the status dot is backed by the word “Available”).
The hand-drawn hint (“hover to know the artist”) and its arrow are aria-hidden, since each card's name already says it shows details; the small thumbnail on the back has alt="".
While a card is turned over, its back shows the same 3px focus ring as the front, since focus stays on the front's button.

items.name: hero-section-04
items.title: Curtains hero section
items.description: A full-bleed architectural photograph cut into vertical curtain slices that open around the pointer with physics easing, over a geometric Syne headline, brand navbar, and detached floating CTA.

useCases: Architecture and design studio home pages
Creative agency and portfolio landing pages
Editorial launch pages leading with photos
Luxury architecture and spatial design sites

a11y.reducedMotion: The opening curtain intro is skipped and the slices start at rest. They don't follow the pointer, a click opens or closes them at once, and the photo still fades from grey to colour.

keyboard.action: Moves through the six nav links and “Inquire”, then the photo; below lg a menu button replaces the links
On the photo, opens or closes the curtain slices; on the menu button, opens or closes the menu
Follows the focused link
Closes the open mobile menu

notes: The headline is an h1 by default (headingLevel 2 for secondary use); the nav sits in a header and the content in a plain div, so the page keeps its single main landmark.
The photo is a focusable element with role="button" that reports aria-expanded, named “Toggle curtain slices: Luminescent green tendrils flowing through darkness” (`imageAlt` folded into the name).
The greyscale copy of the photo and the seam strips are aria-hidden.
The mobile menu button is named “Open navigation menu” or “Close navigation menu” and reports aria-expanded.

items.name: footer-section
items.title: App download footer
items.description: A dark rounded footer for app sites: a red download panel with App Store and Google Play badges and a diagram of the app as a hub with four feature nodes, light running the wires into it, then four link columns, a pinned post, the copyright and social links. Stays dark in light and dark mode.

useCases: Mobile app and music streaming websites
SaaS sites that end with an app download call
Product landing pages with store badges
Startup sites that need a full footer with socials

a11y.reducedMotion: The light beams on the wires and the ripple round the hub are hidden, the hub's equaliser bars stop, and the store badges no longer shrink when pressed.

keyboard.action: Moves through the two store badges, the 14 column links, the pinned post and the three social links.
Follows the focused link.

notes: The headline “Connect. Don't Just Listen” is an h2; each link column is a nav landmark named after its title (“Platform”, “Company”, “Resources”, “Legal”), though the titles themselves are plain text, not headings.
The store badges are links named “Download on the App Store” and “Get it on Google Play”; the icon-only social links are named “Clova on Instagram”, “Clova on Facebook” and “Clova on X”.
The pinned post link reads “Clova, @clovaapp: We've just announced…”: hidden separators keep the name, handle and text apart.
The whole hub diagram, including its node labels, is aria-hidden, as are the brand marks and icons.
gaps: With normal motion settings the beams, hub ripple and equaliser bars loop forever with no pause control; only the reduced-motion setting stops them (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).

items.name: statement-section
items.title: Parted statement
items.description: A big statement parts round a growing image as you scroll, then a second statement rises out of the photo.

useCases: Brand stories and manifesto sections
Agency, studio and fashion websites
Launch pages that need a cinematic moment

a11y.reducedMotion: Nothing moves: scroll is followed directly, the lines stay parted round the small circle and fade out, the circle crossfades into the whole photo instead of growing, and the second statement only fades in.
notes: The full statement is a visually hidden h2 (h1 with headingLevel={1}) and the second statement a hidden paragraph, so each is read once; the moving word copies are aria-hidden.
The photo is a real image named by `image.alt` (“Wind turbines against the rising sun”); the still copy used for the reduced-motion crossfade has empty alt, so it's read once.
The eyebrow “(02) — Field notes” is plain visible text and is read as written.
It has nothing to focus; keyboard users pass through it by scrolling, and it stays pinned for three screen heights by default (the length prop).
A change to the reduced-motion setting takes effect at once, without a reload.

items.name: hero-section-05
items.title: Case study hero
items.description: A project page header for studios on one 6-column grid: the project's name and story, a row of details and three photos, with a live studio clock and an entrance that builds the page row by row.

useCases: Case study pages for architecture studios
Project pages for design and brand agencies
Portfolio pages for photographers
Work pages that lead with photos and credits

a11y.reducedMotion: No rising title, opening photos or zoom: everything fades in over 200ms, the clock's digits swap in place, and the link arrows and underline don't move on hover.

keyboard.action: Moves through the studio name, the main links, Start a project, All projects and All photos.
Follows the focused link.

notes: The project's name is the page's h1; the details are a description list (label and value), and every photo has alt text from its `alt` prop.
The current main link is marked with aria-current="page".
The clock is read after the page loads and every 15 seconds; screen readers get the whole time, not the rolling digits.
Below the md breakpoint the main links and the clock are hidden, and the third photo is left out; its link stays.
gaps: On phones the main links are hidden with no menu to reach them; add your own menu if the section is your page's only navigation. (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)

items.name: feature-sphere-section
items.title: Feature index sphere
items.description: An editorial index of features in big type beside a live WebGL image sphere: choose a feature and its images fly out of the sphere into a pile.

useCases: Agency and studio services pages
Product feature overviews with imagery
Editorial and portfolio websites

a11y.reducedMotion: The index lines and descriptions change without easing. The sphere stops turning by itself, images jump straight into and out of the pile, and it stops when you let go of a drag. A setting change applies at once.

keyboard.action: Moves through the five feature buttons; the open feature's “View work” link comes right after its button.
Opens the focused feature: its description unfolds and its images fly into the pile.
Moves focus to the previous or next feature button, wrapping at the ends.
Moves focus to the first or last feature button.

notes: A visually hidden h2, “What we do”, names the section; each feature name is an h3 holding a button with aria-expanded.
The open feature's button is aria-disabled (read as unavailable) because one feature always stays open; closed descriptions are inert, so their text and links are skipped.
The link reads “View work: Architecture”, with the feature name added as hidden text; the row numbers are hidden from screen readers.
The sphere's canvas is hidden; the open feature's images are listed by their alt text in a hidden list, and a polite live region announces changes such as “Aviation: 8 images”.

items.name: feature-section-02
items.title: Developer tool features
items.description: A big headline over three cards, each with a detailed drawing of its claim: a DevTools page-weight treemap, a code editor with its deployment on top and one visitor's journey, step by step. Follows your light and dark theme.

useCases: SaaS and analytics product landing pages
Developer tool feature overviews
Product pages that explain an approach in three points

a11y.reducedMotion: It doesn't animate by default, so nothing changes. When a card has an `href`, its arrow nudges on hover only when motion is allowed.
notes: The headline is an h2 by default (`headingLevel` sets 1–3) and each card title is one level below it; the three cards are a list.
The three drawings are hidden from screen readers, so each card's claim comes from its title and description.
When a card has an `href`, its title becomes a link stretched over the whole card, and the card shows a focus outline while the link has focus.

items.name: feature-section-03
items.title: Isometric feature grid
items.description: A big headline and lead beside a 2 × 2 grid of features, each with a detailed isometric drawing on a warm paper tile, framed by crop marks.

useCases: E-commerce and logistics landing pages
Fulfillment, shipping and Shopify app websites
Product pages with illustrated feature grids

a11y.reducedMotion: It doesn't animate, so nothing changes.
notes: The headline is an h2 by default (headingLevel sets 1–3), and each feature title takes the next level down, so the four titles are h3s.
The features are a real list (ul/li), each with its title and description as text.
Every drawing, the parcel badge in the headline and the crop marks are aria-hidden, so the words on the truck and flag (“Parcel”, “Tue 14”) aren't read; the titles carry the meaning.
The dashed guide lines are decorative separators that screen readers skip; the small numbers “01”–“04” are plain text read just before each title.

items.name: feature-section-04
items.title: Security features with device
items.description: A headline beside a phone on a blurred landscape and a masonry of five feature tiles, each with a tinted, engraved icon plate.

useCases: Crypto wallet and fintech app websites
Security and privacy feature pages
Mobile app landing pages with a device mockup

a11y.reducedMotion: It doesn’t animate, so nothing changes.
notes: The headline is an h2 by default (headingLevel sets 1 to 3), and each feature title is one level below it, inside two lists of tiles.
The blurred background photo has empty alt text, and the phone mockup (including its on-screen text), icon plates and engraving are SVGs marked aria-hidden.
Screen readers get the headline, the intro and the five feature titles with their descriptions, in that order.

items.name: feature-section-05
items.title: AI context features
items.description: Two product windows on one tray: a chart of how fast a snapshot of your knowledge goes stale, and a chat whose answer names the file it read.

useCases: AI assistant and knowledge-base product pages
Enterprise search and RAG platform landing pages
Developer tools that keep docs in sync with code
Product pages that compare a live system with a stale one

a11y.reducedMotion: Nothing plays: the chart is drawn complete with no line-end pulse, the chat shows its whole answer with a fade only and no shimmer, the windows swap without sliding, and the crosshair jumps.

keyboard.action: Moves to the “Live context” link, the chart's slider, then the “Traceable answers” link.
On the chart, steps to the next change and shows it as a diff.
On the chart, steps to the previous change.
On the chart, jumps ten changes forward or back.
On the chart, jumps to the first or the last change.
Closes the change details.
Follows the focused column-title link.

notes: The section title is an h2 by default and the two column titles are h3 links, “Live context” and “Traceable answers”.
The chart drawing is aria-hidden; a screen-reader sentence gives the totals: share still live, the snapshot's share, the number of changes and the sources.
The slider “Changes since the snapshot” reads each change in words: date, file, who changed it, the old and new line, and the snapshot's share at that point.
In the chat, the question and answer carry hidden “Question:” and “Answer:” prefixes, the chips are a list named “Sources”, and the “Reading 4 sources” shimmer is hidden.
Tabbing into the chart brings its window to the front, and tabbing out of it brings the chat back.

items.name: brands-section
items.title: Brand roster showcase
items.description: A rolling list of brand names: the lit one opens its products beside it, sliding the way you move.

useCases: Marketplaces and multi-brand stores
Concept and department store homepages
Wholesale platforms showing who they stock
Retail landing pages featuring partner brands

a11y.reducedMotion: Nothing cycles by itself, and the “Show more brands” button shows under the rows. Pointing at or tabbing to a row still lights it, but the name, thumbnail, products and caption swap instantly, with no roll, slide or blur.

keyboard.action: Moves to “Browse all brands”, the seven brand links (focus lights one and holds the cycle), then “Show more brands”.
Follows the focused link.
On “Show more brands”, swaps the brands waiting in the roster into the rows at once.

notes: The heading is an h2 (“Shop from brands like”) and the brands are a list of links, each named by its brand, like “Kilnworks”.
Each link's description gives the brand's category, product count and its three product photos' alt text, since the photos sit in aria-hidden cells that swap every step; the thumbnail has empty alt.
“Show more brands” is visually hidden until focused (always shown with reduced motion), and a status line reads what it brought in, e.g. “Now showing Morrow, Solen, Quietform, Vale Parfums.”
The caption under the products (brand, category, product count) is plain text and isn't announced when it changes; the same details are in each link's description.
gaps: While on screen, a new row lights up and rolls to another brand every 3 seconds; it pauses only on hover or focus, with no visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).

items.name: arc-carousel
items.title: Arc carousel
items.description: Project names turn on a curved dial beside a linked image: it steps on a spring, drags and flicks by hand with detents, and opens the project in the centre.

useCases: Architecture and design studio websites
Portfolio and selected work pages
Collection and campaign showcases

a11y.reducedMotion: Autoplay starts paused. Steps jump straight to the item instead of springing, the image swaps with no slide, blur or fade, and the speed lean, detent pulse and hover transitions are off.

keyboard.action: Moves to “Pause” (shown only while focused), then the dial, then the “View project: …” image link.
On “Pause”, stops autoplay; the button then reads “Play” and resumes it.
On the dial, steps to the next project.
On the dial, steps to the previous project.
On the dial, jumps to the first or last project.
On the dial or the image link, opens the active project's link.

notes: The block is a region named “Selected projects” with the role description “carousel”, and autoplay pauses while focus or the pointer is inside it.
The dial is a vertical slider of the same name whose value reads like “Quiet Room, 2024, 5 of 6”; the labels drawn on the arc are aria-hidden.
Each image uses its item's alt text, and the link around it is named “View project: <project>”.
Changes made by dragging or tapping are announced through a polite live region; autoplay steps stay silent.
gaps: Autoplay steps every 2.5 s or so without end, and the lasting “Pause” button is only visible while it has keyboard focus, so mouse and touch users can only pause by hovering or dragging (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide).

items.name: word-wheel
items.title: Word wheel
items.description: A centred headline on a picker wheel: words roll through the line to complete “Built for founders”, faded neighbours above and below, in your text size and colour.

useCases: SaaS and startup landing page heroes
Products sold to several kinds of customers
Enterprise sites with a page per industry
Agency and studio home pages

a11y.reducedMotion: It doesn't roll on its own: it holds on the first word with its neighbours faded above and below, and every transition is off.
notes: Screen readers get it as a sentence: the lead (“Built for”), then a list of every audience once; the copies of a short list and the bold duplicate layer are aria-hidden.
The rolling isn't announced: there's no live region, so screen readers aren't interrupted every step.
It renders no heading element; wrap it in your own h1 or h2 when it's the page's headline.

a11y.reducedMotion: Menus and the quick-prompts tray fade without scaling or rising, the tray unfolds at once, and hover pills jump instead of sliding. While listening, the voice bars hold still and “Listening...” stops pulsing.

keyboard.action: Moves through “Quick prompts” (and its six prompts once unfolded), “Message”, then the footer buttons
In “Message”, sends the prompt; “Send” stays disabled while the field is empty
Activates the focused button: picks a prompt, opens a menu, chooses an option or toggles voice input
In the model menu, focusing a model opens its reasoning depths; Tab walks through them before the next model
In the permission menu, focusing a mode shows its description at once
Closes the open attachment, model or permission menu; the model and permission menus return focus to their button

notes: The text field is named “Message”; the icon buttons are named “Add attachment”, “Voice input” or “Stop listening” (with aria-pressed) and “Send”. Each attachment pill has a remove button like “Remove dataset.csv”.

“Quick prompts”, “Add attachment” and the model and permission buttons report aria-expanded; the model button reads e.g. “Quick ChatGPT”. While the tray is folded, its prompts are inert: out of the Tab order and hidden.

The chosen model, reasoning depth and permission mode are marked with aria-pressed. Each permission mode carries its description as its accessible description; tabbing out of the model or permission menu closes it.
Usage limits show the percentage left as text beside each ring, and the menu icons are hidden from screen readers.
While listening, the text field is replaced by a wave and the text “Listening...”.
